briefs.title: Hatch through first bond
briefs.captureObjective: Show a continuous authentic hatch interaction followed by one concrete first bond response, with enough context to distinguish procedural appearance, animation, and any specific remembered state.
briefs.startingState: Clean company-controlled local fixture before the committed hatch action; no entered name or personal save data visible.

requiredBeats.beat: Show the playable pre-hatch state and the player's committed hatch action without a cut.
Show the in-engine reveal long enough to observe the creature's appearance and animation.
Show the player action that creates or tests the first bond response.
Show the concrete game response and stable aftermath; name the exact state only if verified in the build.

claimSupport.boundary: One visible procedural result supports variation, not global uniqueness or collision-free generation.
Use only if the capture names and visibly demonstrates a specific implemented remembered state; animation or affection alone is insufficient.

briefs.accessibilityDraft: A player begins the hatch sequence. An alien creature emerges, animates in the game, and responds to the player's first bonding action.
briefs.expiryTrigger: Hatch, genetics, first-bond, memory, creature animation, UI, or audio behavior changes.

briefs.title: Player-led realm restoration
briefs.captureObjective: Show one legible damaged realm state, the player's relevant action, the restoration transition, and a stable restored state in authentic gameplay.
briefs.startingState: Clean company-controlled fixture at the selected realm before its restoration commitment, with the damaged state clearly visible.

requiredBeats.beat: Establish the damaged realm state and readable environmental difference.
Show the player's relevant action or committed success state.
Show the restoration transition without replacing it with concept or pre-rendered marketing art.
Hold on the stable restored state from a comparable view long enough to understand the change.

claimSupport.boundary: One captured realm supports the restoration mechanic; a separate current-build check must verify the six-realm count.

doesNotProve: that all six realms are complete in the captured build
that every player action permanently changes every realm
procedural or AI generation of the realm
final visual quality on every supported device
briefs.accessibilityDraft: A damaged realm is visible before the player completes the restoring action. The environment transforms and settles into its restored state.
briefs.expiryTrigger: Realm count, selected realm, restoration mechanics, art, UI, transition, or audio changes.

briefs.title: Project Beacon discovery or choice
briefs.captureObjective: Show an authentic Project Beacon discovery or player choice with enough fictional context and immediate game response to understand the tension, without revealing the ending.
briefs.startingState: Clean company-controlled fixture immediately before an approved spoiler-bounded Project Beacon discovery or choice.

requiredBeats.beat: Establish concise in-game Project Beacon context and the available player action.
Show the player making or confirming the discovery or choice.
Show the immediate authored game response without editing in a different consequence.
End before ending spoilers while retaining enough aftermath to understand the narrative tension.

claimSupport.boundary: Supports the Project Beacon premise as fiction; does not establish real science, adaptive narrative, or downstream consequence unless visibly captured.

doesNotProve: branching consequences not visible in the capture
scientific accuracy or a real-world mission
briefs.accessibilityDraft: Project Beacon's mission is presented in the game. The player makes a discovery or choice, and the story responds without revealing the ending.
briefs.expiryTrigger: Project Beacon story, choice, dialogue, consequence, UI, spoiler boundary, or audio changes.
